note: 14 findings, all accepted and fixed in the same iterate. Dispositions inline. The reviewer explicitly reported no finding for categories (d) shared-state on stamp_fixed_point and most of (a) resolver correctness, and confirmed bloat/anti-ratchet clean.

review.finding: no_base short-circuited BEFORE the presence check, so a commitless repository whose Step F also produced nothing returned no_base/exit 0, Step H continued, and verify is skipped on no_base by design. Zero evidence documents shipped with every layer reporting success - bypassing no_documents in exactly the branch that needs it.
review.disposition: FIXED - present/absent computed first; no_documents returns before the base is even resolved. Pinned by test_nothing_to_stamp_at_all_is_reported_rather_than_passing.

review.finding: Step H's status list was presented as exhaustive but omitted no_documents, and its ok bullet over-claimed: ok with a non-empty absent list means an incomplete set, which verify_commit presence-filters and calls verified.
review.disposition: FIXED - list is now explicitly exhaustive and covers ok-with-empty-absent, ok-with-non-empty-absent (do not commit), no_base, no_documents, partial and write_failed.

review.finding: git add -A was newly prescribed with no precondition. Adopt runs on a brownfield repository; an untracked file there was never forced into .gitignore, so a .env, a database dump or a scratch key would be staged into a commit titled 'adopt repository into Shipwright SDLC'. Adopt's own gitignore check classifies only adopt's outputs.
review.disposition: FIXED - a mandatory git status --porcelain inspection precedes the add, with the expected path list named and an instruction to stop and ask on anything else.

review.finding: The remedy named --restore, which /shipwright-compliance does not accept - it is an internal flag of refresh_compliance_docs.py, and Step 2c runs it itself as the first line of the --refresh-pr procedure. An operator typing /shipwright-compliance --restore hits the very circle AC-6 exists to break. The mini-plan's premise misread an internal step as an operator precondition.
review.disposition: FIXED - the remedy names only /shipwright-compliance --fix and --refresh-pr plus the genuine operator-side precondition (commit or stash unrelated work). New test_suggestion_names_only_flags_the_skill_actually_accepts validates every flag in the remedy against the SKILL's accepted-flag list, so this cannot regress.

review.finding: The non-mutating guarantee held for validation but not for write_back itself, which writes the set in a loop with no rollback - a raise on the fourth file leaves three stamped. This mode also returns before the crash handler the other modes have, so the agent would get a traceback with no status field.
review.disposition: FIXED - write wrapped; on OSError the originals (still in the payload) are restored and a write_failed status with restored/unrestored is returned non-zero. Step H gained the matching branch. Pinned by test_a_failed_write_puts_the_originals_back.

review.finding: The resolver validated the TRIMMED value and interpolated the UNTRIMMED one, so a padded --base passed the lexical gate and then failed to resolve, silently degrading an establishable commit to no_base.
review.disposition: FIXED - safe_commit once at the top, the trimmed value used thereafter. Pinned by test_a_padded_base_is_still_accepted.

review.finding: An abbreviated --base that is also a ref name resolves as the REF: for 7-39 hex git tries dwim_ref first and falls back to short-oid only if no ref matched. In a repo with a branch named deadbeef, --base deadbeef stamps that branch's tip - a real, plausible, wrong commit. The docstring claimed symbolic revisions could not get through.
review.disposition: FIXED - full 40-hex required; anything shorter is no_base. commit_at_adoption is always full length, so nothing legitimate is lost and the degradation is unstamped-and-honest rather than stamped-and-wrong. Pinned by test_an_abbreviated_base_is_refused_rather_than_resolved.

review.finding: The new module omitted the unconditional sys.path preamble all four sibling compliance_* modules carry, so its ADR-045 protection was importer-dependent.
review.disposition: FIXED - the same unconditional insert added above the lib imports.

review.finding: expected: len(present) was vacuous - in the ok branch present == set(stamped) by construction, so a consumer comparing them got a guarantee that could not fail.
review.disposition: FIXED - reports len(stampable_paths()), the real expectation.

review.finding: The never-resolves-HEAD guard asserted tuple MEMBERSHIP, so the natural fall-through rev-parse --verify HEAD^{commit} would not match; and in the exercised path git is never reached at all, so the assertion was vacuously true.
review.disposition: FIXED - substring match across all arguments AND an explicit assertion that git is not reached at all, so neither half carries the test alone.

review.finding: The amend repair was verified only for the property it fixes, not the one it must preserve: git commit --amend -- <pathspec> survives as a whole commit only because git overlays the pathspec onto a false index from HEAD, and verify_commit looks at nothing outside the evidence set.
review.disposition: FIXED - asserts an unrelated evidence document and a non-evidence artifact (CLAUDE.md) both survive the amended tree.

review.finding: The handoff banner read 'Evidence: current as of this commit' three lines above 'Commit: <sha>', but the stamp deliberately records the PRE-adoption HEAD. Two different SHAs, in a change whose entire subject is evidence that names its own state honestly.
review.disposition: FIXED - banner now reads 'current as of <short base sha>, the commit onboarding read'.

review.finding: The banner replacement ends in a bare LF while the pattern consumes the original CR, so a CRLF document ends with one LF-only line among CRLF lines. No CI-vs-local divergence found in the delivered tests; the residue is a mixed-ending committed artifact, and a git add failure under core.safecrlf=true.
review.disposition: FILED as trg-00ecedd6, not fixed here. Pre-existing in shared stamping that the release and documents-only-PR paths already depend on; fixing it needs a CRLF fixture and touches two shipping paths, so it is its own change. The escalation (first caller that runs on customer repos where CRLF checkout is normal) is recorded on the card.

review.finding: The AC-5 section was a 15-line essay restating the Step H banner and guide.md in a file whose own footer states every line costs context in every future session of every adopted repository.
review.disposition: FIXED - condensed to the two-answer contrast plus the two commands, about 4 lines. The drift test still passes because it asserts the heading and both commands, all of which survive.
